description: Pebble's shared Renovate preset: weekly, grouped, three-day release age, security fixes any time, auto-merge only for Payload and Next.js patch and security updates

customManagers.description: The toolkit's action and reusable-workflow pins: a SHA with a # @pebbletech/infra@<version> comment, read from the toolkit's release tags. A toolkit-ref input right below the pin (the site-deploy stub) is part of the match, so its SHA moves with the pin's

packageRules.description: Patch and minor updates for everything, one PR. First, so any later group (the ones below, and every group a repo adds) takes its packages out: the last matching rule wins
Majors stay one PR each so the changelog is read. A repo's own group sets matchUpdateTypes ["!major"] to keep this for its packages

Payload: payload and every @payloadcms package share one version, so they move together, majors included. Patches get their own branch (renovate/patch-payload), so a branch GitHub was told to auto-merge never later holds a minor: Renovate does not take auto-merge off a PR
Next.js: next and its @next packages share one version, so they move together, majors included. Patches get their own branch (renovate/patch-next), for the same reason as Payload's
Node and pnpm pins move on purpose, not by bot; by dep name, so setup-node's node-version input is covered too
The toolkit's actions are pinned through the regex manager above, never by the github-actions manager
@pebbletech/infra on npm and the toolkit action pins move together, as soon as a release is out: they are ours
Payload and Next.js patches auto-merge once the required checks pass, unless Renovate marks them breaking (a prerelease step, a 0.x patch); their minors and majors wait for a person

Payload and Next.js security fixes that are a patch or a minor auto-merge once the required checks pass; a major security fix waits for a person. Renovate sets isVulnerabilityAlert from its alert rules, which it appends after every rule here and applies before this rule is read again
